Biological clustering:

- Respiratory / gas exchange: dyspnea, cough, pneumonia, acute hypoxemic respiratory failure, hypoxemia, atelectasis, pleural effusion, lung-field abnormality.
- Renal / metabolic: hypokalemia, acidosis, dehydration, hyponatremia, acute kidney injury, hyperglycemia, hyperkalemia, hypomagnesemia.
- Cardiovascular / hemodynamic: hypotension, tachycardia, chest pain, abnormal ECG, edema, hypertension.
- Gastrointestinal: constipation, diarrhea, abdominal pain, GERD, dysphagia.
- Hematologic / nutrition: anemia, plasma protein disorder, severe protein-calorie malnutrition, undernutrition.
- Inflammatory / infectious: sepsis, fever, pneumonia overlap, immunodeficiency, nonspecific illness.
- Neuropsychiatric / pain: anxiety disorder, disorder of brain, pain.

Interpretation: the post-discharge phenotype is not a single “long COVID” code pattern; it is dominated by pulmonary sequelae plus systemic critical-illness clusters: metabolic/renal derangements, hemodynamic/cardiac symptoms, GI dysfunction, anemia/malnutrition, and infection/inflammation. Percentages are exact-concept incidence, so they likely underestimate broader phenotype families and may include coding/discovery effects after hospitalization.
